We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Electrically charged black holes with electroweak hair
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct electrically charged black holes in Einstein's gravity coupled to the bosonic sector of the electroweak theory, focusing on static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions, with the weak mixing angle fixed to its Standard Model value. Horizon regularity imposes a resonance condition relating the charged-vector frequency to the electromagnetic potential at the horizon, corresponding to the threshold of charged superradiance. A perturbative analysis further shows that nonextremal Reissner-Nordström black holes do not support regular, exponentially localized, spherically symmetric electroweak clouds satisfying such condition. Thus, the hairy solutions cannot emerge via a bifurcation from this electrovacuum family. Moreover, our numerical investigation reveals two apparently disconnected families of bosonic stars. Within the explored parameter space, the hairy black holes are connected to the strongly gravitating one.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Bouncing and QNM convergence in Kerr
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that the convergence region of the QNM representation of the retarded Green's function of the Kerr spacetime is set by complex-time bouncing singularities, as in our previous work for the Schwarzschild case. The main difference between Kerr and Schwarzschild is that there are two distinct QNM families, prolate and oblate, which have different convergence regions. We provide explicit analytical formulae for the bounce radii and corresponding convergence regions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates. We also provide an analysis of convergence in the Reissner-Nordström spacetime.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Mercury (Hg): a relativistic $N$-body simulation for Horndeski gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present Mercury, a relativistic $N$-body code for cosmological simulations in the $α$-basis formulation of Horndeski gravity. Mercury extends a particle-mesh scheme by incorporating the dynamics of the additional scalar degree of freedom and the corresponding modified Einstein equations, expressed in terms of the time-dependent functions $α_{\rm K}, α_{\rm B}, α_{\rm M}, α_{\rm T}$ and the effective Planck mass $M_*^2$. This generalises our previous implementation of Horndeski subclass models, namely $k$-essence and kinetic gravity braiding (KGB), to the general linear Horndeski $α$-basis. The code evolves the additional scalar degree of freedom and its effective stress--energy tensor alongside the nonlinear matter and metric fields, so that nonlinear structure formation sources the scalar-field evolution and feeds back on the gravitational potentials. Through its interface with hi_class, Mercury supports both phenomenological $α$-function parametrisations and covariant Horndeski theories; we demonstrate the latter using nKGB, the Cubic Galileon, and Brans--Dicke models. We validate the implementation against hi_class in the linear regime and recover the expected nonlinear $k$-essence and KGB limits. For the luminal Horndeski models considered here, we show how a running effective Planck mass generates gravitational slip through the scalar anisotropic stress and modifies the friction terms governing the vector and tensor metric perturbations. The evolution of $M_*^2$ also modifies the normalisation and scale dependence of the effective dark-energy density contrast, leaving a corresponding imprint on its power spectrum. The present framework provides an intermediate step towards nonlinear Horndeski simulations, in which nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening effects can be incorporated consistently within the same relativistic framework.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The direct wave component of black hole (BH) ringdown, revealed through quasinormal-mode filters, carries a non-quasinormal-mode imprint of the plunging perturber's dynamics. However, the connection between the source trajectory and the observed direct wave remains incompletely understood. We first show that the full waveform filtered by the frequency-dependent black hole response gives a substantially more localized kernel than the standard rational filter approach. We then show that analytically continuing the Teukolsky source variables to complex coordinates allows for a semianalytic direct wave which closely reproduces numerical integration throughout the entire plunge. Our generalized steepest-descent method clarifies how coherent emission shapes the imprint of source dynamics on the observed direct wave beyond the light-cone picture.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, plus Supplemental Material. To be submitted to Physical Review D Letters

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent's successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nonlinear gauge maps and the structure of Goldstone loops in canonical inflation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We clarify the nonlinear relation between the spatially flat scalar and Goldstone descriptions of canonical single-field inflation. An exact clock map shows how potential interactions are reorganized into derivative Goldstone interactions. A change of slicing further connects their dilation symmetry to its comoving realization. We then study the Goldstone two-point function at one loop in the decoupling limit. Using identities derived from the general mode equation, we reveal how seemingly independent loop contributions combine and their non-boundary parts cancel once the associated counterterms are included. This reduction requires no explicit mode-function solution. The leading adiabatic long-mode response reduces to a total derivative in loop momentum, which requires an additional regularization prescription.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Surrogate model of gravitational waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries based on the hybridization of WaSABI-C inspirals with numerical relativity waveforms
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: With the incorporation of aligned-spin dynamics into self-force waveform models, such as the WaSABI-C inspiral model, and with the release of the SXS collaboration's third public catalog of NR simulations, the gravitational waveform modeling community has made significant advances in the modeling of spinning, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries. In light of these developments, we present WaSABINRHybSur2dq15, the first surrogate model to incorporate information from self-force theory, post-Newtonian theory, and numerical relativity. The model is trained on 65 hybrid waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries with mass ratios spanning 1:1.25 to 1:20 and aligned-spins for the primary black hole ranging -0.5 to 0.5. The hybrid waveforms are generated from a set of WaSABI-C inspirals and NR waveforms from the third SXS public catalog. The model covers the parameter domain $1.25 \leq q \leq 15$ and $|χ_{1z}| \leq 0.5$, and includes the $(2,2),\, (2,1),\, (3,3),\, (4,4),$ and $(5,5)$ spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes. The model also spans the entire LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) frequency band (with $f_{\text{low}}=20$ Hz) for total masses $M \gtrsim 111.5\,M_{\odot}$. We find that the WaSABINRHybSur2dq15 model faithfully reproduces the hybrid waveforms with mismatches less than $10^{-3}$ for total masses in the range $80\,M_{\odot} \leq M \leq 300\,M_{\odot}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Collapsar-Disk Origin for GW190814
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: GW190814 was a remarkable gravitational-wave (GW) event: a merger between a $23 M_\odot$ black hole (BH) and a $2.6\,M_\odot$ compact object, with an extreme mass ratio that is difficult to reproduce through standard isolated-binary or dynamical formation channels. Recent work has shown that neutrino-cooled collapsar disks can become gravitationally unstable and fragment, producing neutron stars (NSs) or low-mass BHs in orbit around the newly formed central BH. These fragments may subsequently interact, scatter, merge with one another, or inspiral into the central remnant. We explore the possibility that GW190814 originated from such a collapsar-disk fragment merging with the central BH. A key prediction of this scenario is a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova preceding the GW event, and we identify the Type Ib supernova candidate SN2019npv, which occurred inside the GW190814 credible volume approximately 60 days before coalescence, as a possible electromagnetic precursor. Although this delay is too long for a conventional kilonova counterpart, we show that three-body interactions among disk fragments can excite some compact objects to wide orbits and produce merger delays of weeks to months. While GW190814 itself was not expected to produce detectable tidal-disruption-powered emission, future delayed mergers in this channel could generate luminous transients through either reprocessed kilonova heating or shocks driven as merger ejecta collide with the preceding supernova ejecta. Finally, treating SN2019npv as the electromagnetic counterpart makes GW190814 a bright standard siren and yields $H_{0} = 71.1^{+9.3}_{-7.5} km s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 29 pages, submission includes zip file with ancillary material

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Mass inflation and the $C^2$-inextendibility of spherically symmetric charged scalar field dynamical black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
It has long been suggested that the Cauchy horizon of dynamical black holes is subject to a weak null singularity, under the mass inflation scenario. We study in spherical symmetry the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations and \textit{while we do not directly show mass inflation}, we obtain a "mass inflation/ridigity" dichotomy. More precisely, we prove assuming (sufficiently slow) decay of the charged scalar field on the event horizon, that the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}= \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$ for two (possibly empty) disjoint connected sets $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{S}$ such that:
  _$\mathcal{D}$ (the dynamical set) is a past set on which the Hawking mass blows up (mass inflation scenario).
  _$\mathcal{S}$ (the static set) is a future set isometric to a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon i.e.\ the radiation is zero on $\mathcal{S}$.
  As a consequence, we establish a novel classification of Cauchy horizons into three types: dynamical ($\mathcal{S}=\emptyset$), static ($\mathcal{D}=\emptyset$) or mixed, and prove that $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}$ is globally $C^2$-inextendible. Our main motivation is the $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture for a realistic model of spherical collapse in which charged matter emulates the repulsive role of angular momentum: in our case the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon system on one-ended space-times. As a result, we prove in spherical symmetry that:
  - two-ended asymptotically flat space-times are $C^2$-future-inextendible i.e. $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship is true for Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon, assuming the decay of the scalar field on the event horizon at the expected rate.
  - In the one-ended case, the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $C^2$-inextendible. This result suppresses the main obstruction to $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship in spherical collapse.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Strengthened the event-horizon assumptions to account for the correction to the instability argument in arXiv:1704.05790

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the Rényi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second Rényi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Measuring the Neutron-Star Moment of Inertia using Nonlinear Orbital Variations from Lense-Thirring Precession
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A future measurement of Lense-Thirring (LT) precession using a binary radio pulsar is expected to yield the pulsar's moment of inertia ($I_{\rm p}$). However, most of the known pulsar-binary systems expected to provide this opportunity will exhibit linear variations in the orbital elements, due to LT precession, that are difficult to separate from distance-dependent variations induced by other mechanisms. In this work, we demonstrate that the pulsar-timing signature of LT precession for an arbitrary orbital orientation produces nonlinear orbital variations after a sufficient amount of time; if detected, these nonlinear variations provide a means to constrain $I_{\rm p}$ without the need for independent measurements of orbital geometry or distance. We show through simulations that these nonlinear signatures are indeed detectable in pulsar-binary systems with an appropriate combination of timing precision and orbital geometry. Our simulations also show that nonlinear orbital variations from LT precession are expected to be detectable in PSR J1757$-$1854 and that its $I_{\rm p}$ can be constrained to precision as high as 10% by 2040 even without knowledge of distance.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Resubmitted during September 2026; comments welcome!

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Stability of Homogeneous minimal hypersurfaces in the Page space and $Y^{p,q}$ Sasaki-Einstein manifolds
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the stability of homogeneous minimal submanifolds in two families of closed Einstein manifolds, the Page space $\mathbb{CP}^2 \# \overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ and the Sasaki-Einstein spaces $Y^{p,q}$, which are equipped with cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics admitting the isometric action of $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and $U(1) \times U(1) \times SU(2)$ respectively. We determine all the homogeneous, minimal hypersurfaces and explicitly compute the spectrum of their associated stability operators and determine their index.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 13 pages, 1 figure; v2 (agrees with published version): 15 pages, 4 figures, substantial improvements and statement of Theorem 1.2 corrected

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact Regular Planar Black Holes solutions in Bumblebee gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. We consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. The field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. Found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. Analytical expressions for this functions has been found. This solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Regular black holes with Minkowskian cores: energy-condition obstruction and optical screening
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct an asymptotically flat black-hole geometry with a Minkowskian core using gravitational decoupling and analyze its static and rotating extensions. Rather than imposing global energy-condition viability, we show that the vanishing central density required by the Minkowskian core produces a local null-energy-condition obstruction for the present static closure class. The exact mass profile can be written in terms of the regularized incomplete gamma function, which makes transparent both the horizon structure and the exponential localization of the deformation. This localization yields an analytic optical-screening mechanism: on the black-hole branch, deviations of the critical impact parameter from Schwarzschild are controlled by the exponentially suppressed mass deficit at the photon sphere. We also clarify the status of the rotating extension: curvature invariants remain finite on the physical domain $r\geq0$, but this local statement does not by itself establish a globally regular analytic extension through the Kerr disk. These results separate local core regularization from global completeness and explain why strong modifications of the interior can coexist with very small changes in exterior optical observables.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gauge-invariant quantum gravitational corrections to correlation functions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A recent proposal for gauge-invariant observables in inflation [R. Brunetti et al., JHEP 1608 (2016) 032] is examined. We give a generalisation of their construction to general background spacetimes. In flat space, we calculate one-loop graviton corrections to a scalar two-point function in a general gauge for the graviton. We explicitely show how the gauge-dependent terms cancel between the usual self-energy contributions and the additional corrections inherent in these observables. The one-loop corrections have the expected functional form, contrary to another recently studied proposal for gauge-invariant observables [M. B. Fröb, Class. Quant. Grav. 35 (2018) 035005] where this is not the case. Furthermore, we determine the one-loop graviton corrections to the four-point coupling of the gauge-invariant scalar field, and the corresponding running of the coupling constant induced by graviton loops. Interestingly, the $β$ function is negative for most values of the non-minimal coupling of the scalar field to curvature, including minimal and conformal coupling.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 34 pages, 1 figure, calculational errors corrected, includes corrigendum to published article as separate TeX file

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Eccentricity Distribution for Dynamical Gravitational-Wave Merger Channels in The Pinhole Regime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We argue that various dynamical astrophysical black hole merger channels are expected to result in a common eccentricity distribution at gravitational-wave (GW) frequencies relevant for LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA (LVK) in the high eccentricity limit. This follows from the large separation of scales between the GW regime required for creating eccentric mergers in LVK, and the underlying astrophysical formation environment. Our analytical solution shows exceptional agreement with numerical studies. This finding has important implications for both theoretical studies and ongoing searches for eccentric GW sources.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nonexistence of Multiple Black Holes in Stationary Analytic Vacuum spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We prove the nonexistence of non-rotating and degenerate horizon components in the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum spacetime. This result rules out the final case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes. Consequently, the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is settled affirmatively in full.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole -approaching a sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström background fast enough at infinity- in presence of a massive and charged scalar field, motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in that setting :
  1. Stability : We prove that spherically symmetric characteristic initial data to the Einstein-Maxwell- Klein-Gordon equations approaching a Reissner-Nordström background with a sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon in a neighbourhood of time-like infinity. Moreover if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. This generalizes the celebrated stability result of Dafermos for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry.
  2. Instability : We prove that for the class of space-times considered in the stability part, whose scalar field in addition obeys a polynomial averaged-L^2 (consistent) lower bound on the event horizon, the scalar field obeys an integrated lower bound transversally to the Cauchy horizon. As a consequence we prove that the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. This generalizes an instability result due to Luk and Oh for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry.
  This instability of the black hole interior can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Correction of the instability argument, which requires an additional assumption on the event horizon. This additional assumption, like the previous ones, is conjectured to hold for generic exterior perturbations

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Entanglement in the Schwinger effect
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We analyze entanglement generated by the Schwinger effect using a mode-by-mode formalism for scalar and spinor QED in constant backgrounds. Starting from thermal initial states, we derive compact, closed-form results for bipartite entanglement between particle-antiparticle partners in terms of the Bogoliubov coefficients. For bosons, thermal fluctuations enhance production but suppress quantum correlations: the logarithmic negativity is nonzero only below a (mode-dependent) critical temperature $T_c$. At fixed $T$, entanglement appears only above a critical field $E_{\text{entang}}$. For fermions, we observe a qualitatively different pattern: the fermionic logarithmic negativity is non-vanishing at finite temperature, and is monotonically suppressed by thermal noise. As a function of the electric field, it is non-monotonic, featuring a temperature-independent optimal field strength $E_*$ and decreasing on both sides of the maximum. We give quantitative estimates for analog experiments, where our entanglement criteria convert directly into concrete temperature and electric field constraints. These findings identify realistic regimes where the quantum character of Schwinger physics may be tested in the laboratory.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: In v2: fermionic section updated to include the fermionic logarithmic negativity; conclusions and related figures changed accordingly. New references added. In v3: corrected equations and typos; updated references and acknowledgments. 36 pages and 7 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged Rényi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 56 pages, 9 figures, 1 table; v2: probe-limit condition for the attenuation corrected, pole-skipping points added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Integrable mass of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The nontrivial asymptotic structure of rotating black holes in the Bertotti-Robinson universe complicates a direct determination of their conserved mass, leading previous studies to rely on a priori thermodynamic input. We address this long-standing problem using integrability methods, establish local analytic existence and uniqueness via the Cauchy-Kovalevskaja theorem, and obtain a closed expression via a rescaled recurrence whose termination is proved at all orders. The resulting Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson mass coincides with the expression previously derived using the canonical first law identity and reproduces the masses of both Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson subcases. With the mass thus fixed without invoking thermodynamic relations for the first time, we rigorously establish the first law of black-hole thermodynamics and the Smarr formula for a whole family of Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black holes suitable for future applications.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Construction of an analytic multi-component accretion environment and its application to Kerr black hole imaging
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The construction of accretion environments is fundamental to black hole imaging. From a purely geometric perspective, we construct a novel analytic accretion environment comprising a geometrically thick disk, ring-like bumps with a Gaussian profile, and localized compact emission regions modeled by Gaussian distributions. This environment offers high flexibility, enabling independent adjustments of disk thickness, vertical structure, and the positions and morphologies of localized spots, thereby allowing it to qualitatively mimic high-energy astrophysical phenomena. Applying this model to the Kerr spacetime, we investigate the resulting images via radiative transfer and ray-tracing simulations. The results confirm the effectiveness of the numerical implementation and reveal novel observational signatures of Kerr black holes under multi-component illumination, including multiple bright spots and arc-like structures. This work provides a convenient and fully analytic framework for modeling accretion in curved spacetimes, and offers a new perspective on inferring accretion mechanisms and transient high-energy processes from image features.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 25 pages, 19 figures, accepted for publication in EPJC

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes in semiclassical gravity with trace anomaly
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Semiclassical gravity provides a promising framework to address the black hole singularity problem through quantum backreaction characterized by a coupling parameter, making it essential to thoroughly explore the accretion properties around such objects. In this paper, within the framework of semiclassical gravity with type-A trace anomaly, we investigate the thermal radiative signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes across diverse parameter spaces, focusing on the energy flux density, temperature profile, and thermal luminosity. Our findings demonstrate that the introduction of a positive coupling parameter suppresses disk emission, leading to lower peak values of both energy flux density and temperature, as well as lower peak values and corresponding peak frequencies in thermal luminosity compared to their Kerr counterparts in general relativity. In particular, this discrepancy becomes remarkably pronounced when the black hole possesses a high spin. Mechanistically, increasing the coupling parameter reinforces the effective gravitational field strength of the central compact object, which pushes the equatorial stable circular orbits outward and increases the specific energy of the orbiting matter, thereby reducing the radiative efficiency and weakening the overall disk emission. This suppression mechanism offers a potential astrophysical window to distinguish semiclassical gravity from general relativity and to place observational constraints on the coupling parameter via thermal disk spectra.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in Chinese Physics C

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordström and Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The imprint of individual neutron star spins on ejecta, $r$-process nucleosynthesis, and kilonovae in binary neutron star mergers
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: To leading order, the gravitational-wave (GW) signal from binary neutron stars depends on the individual spins, $χ_1$ and $χ_2$, only through the effective spin parameter $χ_{\rm eff}$. We present the first systematic investigation of individual-spin effects on ejecta, $r$-process nucleosynthesis, and kilonova emission, including comparisons at fixed total mass, mass ratio and $χ_{\rm eff}$. We use numerical relativity ejecta from three total mass regimes with the finite-temperature, composition-dependent SFHo equation of state and neutrino emission and absorption. For $M_{\rm tot}=2.55\,M_\odot$ at fixed $χ_{\rm eff}=0$, individual spins change the dynamical ejecta mass by a factor of ${\sim}45$, while the absolute $A\geq140$ yield spans more than two orders of magnitude and the lanthanide to light $r$-process mass ratio increases from ${\sim}2$ to ${\sim}70$. Prompt-collapse $4.10\,M_\odot$ models show heavy-element yield differences exceeding four orders of magnitude at $χ_{\rm eff}=0$. The kilonova retains the individual-spin imprint, with peak brightness differences reaching ${\sim}0.9$ mag. At $40\,{\rm Mpc}$, all three fixed $χ_{\rm eff}=0$ pairs remain above adopted depths at common epochs for all viewing angles, with same-epoch colour differences reaching ${\sim}1.5$ mag. The colour imprint persists when the simulation-derived secular ejecta are replaced by the same parametric disc outflow, indicating that disc mass differences are not the primary driver and that dynamical ejecta make an important contribution. Neutrino absorption systematically brightens the kilonova and shifts peak-associated colours blueward. These EM signatures can break the degeneracy between individual spins in the GW signal.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Quantum Noise Fraction and the addressable fraction in High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The quantum noise fraction $β$, the share of a detector's noise power that is quantum in origin, sets a ceiling $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 1/\sqrt{1-β}$ on the sensitivity improvement that removing quantum-origin noise can yield. In the kHz--GHz band the readout degree of freedom is a bosonic mode and $β= 1/(2\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}+1)$, with $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}$ the Bose--Einstein occupation. Quantum noise then dominates only on the cold side of the thermal frontier $k_BT\ln 3 = \hbarω$ (above 229 MHz at 10 mK), which governs mechanical resonators and electromagnetic cavities alike; a real readout turns it into a joint condition on the occupation and on the excess noise of the readout chain. On a multimode acoustic antenna the frontier can be observed within one device, since the logarithmic slope of $\sqrt{S_hQ}$ along the odd-overtone comb increases by one half across it whatever the dependence of the quality factor on overtone number. On this antenna, crossing the frontier costs more in classical sensitivity than quantum enhancement returns. For a GHz mode of an existing bulk acoustic wave device at 10 mK, $β= 0.984$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$. That ceiling cannot be reached with a linear readout, because with intrinsic damping the zero-point term is the force noise of the bath, fixed by the fluctuation--dissipation theorem. The addressable fraction $β_a$ excludes it: at the standard quantum limit the same mode has $β= 0.992$ but $β_a = 0.496$, an available improvement of 1.41 against a ceiling of 11.0. An array of $10^4$ such devices cross-correlated for one year reaches $3.6\times 10^{-24}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ for an integration bandwidth equal to the linewidth; even granting $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$ in full, a factor $1.0\times 10^{10}$ above the big-bang-nucleosynthesis bound remains, and it is classical.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 37 pages, 3 figures. Accepted Manuscript of the article published in Class. Quantum Grav. 43 (2026) 215005. Data and code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.19862916

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nucleating an Inflationary Universe: Euclidean Wormholes and their No-Boundary Limit
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: No-boundary instantons and Euclidean "wineglass" wormholes have both been proposed as providing suitable initial conditions for the current expanding phase of our universe, and in particular for providing conditions that are favorable to an inflationary phase. These finite action solutions have generally been regarded as unrelated, and enacting different scenarios - in one case the creation of spacetime from nothing, and in the other up-tunneling from a Euclidean Anti-de Sitter vacuum. By studying explicit solutions of both axionic and magnetic wineglass wormholes, we find that in the zero-charge limit the throat of the wormholes pinches off, leaving a no-boundary instanton that disconnects from the asymptotic Anti-de Sitter region. Thus wormholes and no-boundary instantons are part of a common family of Euclidean solutions. Along the way, we resolve the long-known puzzle that the action of wineglass wormholes can become negative. Moreover, small-charge wormholes lead to a longer inflationary phase than large-charge solutions, while no-boundary instantons dominate the probability distribution overall.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 9 pages, v2: typo fixed and equation added, v3: replaced with published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraints on Rastall gravity from current observational data
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the cosmological features of Rastall gravity, where the covariant energy-momentum conservation is modified to $\nabla_μT^μ_ν=λ\nabla_νR$ in curved spacetime. For this purpose, we obtain the modified field equations of Rastall model to linear order of perturbations, and then inspect the evolutionary behavior of cosmological observables, chiefly the matter power spectrum and the Hubble parameter, within the context of Rastall gravity. We also compare Rastall model with cosmological probes, namely cosmic microwave background, weak lensing, supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and redshift-space distortions data. According to our numerical results, Rastall gravity prefers lower growth of structures compared to the $Λ$CDM model, which indicates consistency with low-redshift large-scale structure probes. Moreover, numerical analysis reveals that Rastall gravity with a cosmological constant as the dark energy component suffers from the Hubble tension, like the $Λ$CDM model.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Scalar Vacuum Polarization in Loop Quantum Gravity Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A quantum macroscopic ``Kruskal'' black hole solution that incorporates quantum geometry effects has been derived in \chg{loop quantum gravity} as the counterpart to the classical Schwarzschild solution with a distinct imprint outside the event horizon, even at scales much larger than the Planck length. This resulting black hole quantum geometry is supported by an effective energy density of quantum origin, outside the horizon, which prevents asymptotic flatness at large distances and confines massive particles to finite radii, thereby preventing their escape to infinity. In this work\chg{,} we adapt to these solutions the extended Anderson-Candelas-Christensen-DeWitt approach to compute the quantum vacuum polarization in order to provide an accurate measure of the quantum activity around these black holes. We carry out a numerical implementation of the formalism and present, to our knowledge for the first time, the scalar vacuum polarization $\langleφ^2\rangle$ exterior to this quantum-corrected geometry. We find that the quantum-gravity exponent $ε$ enhances the near-horizon polarization and induces, farther out, a small negative tail that we identify---through a parameter-free \chg{DeWitt-Schwinger} comparison---with the field's response to the nonzero curvature of the background (absent for Ricci-flat Schwarzschild). The correction scales linearly with $ε$, the parameter tracking the quantum gravitational corrections, so that\chg{,} for astrophysically realistic (i.e., tiny) $ε$, the result is numerically indistinguishable from Schwarzschild. The calculation furnishes a consistency check on the quantum activity around these solutions, the fluctuations tracking the local curvature without anomalous growth in the exterior.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Hunting Dark Matter with the Einstein Telescope
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Too light primordial black holes evaporate and are therefore strongly constrained by various bounds, e.g. Cosmic Microwave Background distortion. However, if they are formed strongly clustered, the corresponding haloes may collapse into heavier black holes which may form the entirety of the dark matter of the universe. The indirect signal of such a scenario is the production of a flat stochastic background of gravitational waves which is detectable by the Einstein Telescope.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Mach's principle in atomic transitions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the atomic transition probabilities in atom-mirror set-ups that are in circular motion. In one scenario, the atom is in circular motion inside a static cylindrical mirror. In the other scenario, the cylindrical mirror rotates around its central axis while the atom remains static. We report structural similarity in the atomic transition probabilities between these two cases -- these probabilities are equivalent upon interchanging the field frequencies between the two scenarios. We interpret such an observation as a semi-classical phenomenon analogous to the classical Mach's principle.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Revised version, Published in: Phys. Lett. A 600 (2026) 132303

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quantum States Prepared by Wormholes: Long-Wavelength Deviations from Bunch-Davies
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
Wineglass wormholes mediate the nucleation of baby universes out of an asymptotically Anti-de Sitter or flat spacetime. Upon materialization, the new universe naturally undergoes an inflationary phase. Here we study the quantum state of tensor and probe scalar field fluctuations that these wormhole geometries prepare, finding that they reproduce the Bunch-Davies vacuum for short-wavelength modes but lead to deviations from Bunch-Davies on large scales. These deviations, which depend on the charge of the wormhole, cause a small shift as well as oscillations in the angular power spectrum generated by an ensuing inflationary phase, and thus provide a distinctive cosmological observable.
  The wormholes are supported by either axionic or magnetic charges. In the limit of vanishing charge, they undergo a topological transition after which they contain no-boundary instantons. We find that the small-charge limit suppresses deviations from the Bunch-Davies state for both scalar and tensor fluctuations, indicating that the topological transition is smooth.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, v2: replaced with published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+ω$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordström Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Tribute to S. Deser: Conserved Quantities in Generic Gravity Theories
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: I describe parts of my joint work with S. Deser [March 19, 1931 - April 21, 2023] which started when I was working as a post-doc at Brandeis University in 2001. Our work was mostly, but not exclusively, on conserved charges of higher curvature theories of gravity. I also describe some recent developments, such as expressing the conserved charges in terms of the linearized Riemann tensor; I expound upon the computations. I also reminisce about our interaction for over two decades that went beyond our scientific collaboration. The physics part of this review is intended for graduate students and researchers interested in extended theories of gravity, especially about the conserved quantities and perturbative techniques in these theories.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 1 figure, 39 pages. The section containing the author's reminiscence of S. Deser was published in "The Supersymmetric World: The Beginnings of the Theory", 2nd ed., edited by G. Kane and M. Shifman (World Scientific, Singapore, 2025)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraints on the number of inner horizons from gravitational Noether charges
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A central question in the study of black hole interiors is how matter and geometry constrain the number of horizons. In Einstein gravity, one known method is to use the ADM decomposition of the field equations to derive a differential inequality for the lapse, which then constrains the possible existence of multiple inner horizons. We show that the same obstruction can instead be formulated through the Komar integral as a bulk-boundary balance of gravitational Noether charge. In higher-curvature gravity, a direct ADM analysis becomes more complicated, whereas the gravitational Noether charge naturally retains this bulk-boundary structure. We naturally apply the gravitational Noether charge analysis to Lovelock gravity. We introduce a TCC-like curvature condition and prove that, together with the thermodynamically motivated assumption of positive Wald entropy, it allows at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon inside a nondegenerate event horizon. This suggests that the obstruction reflects a compatibility between bulk gravitational response and horizon thermodynamics.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational Dark Matter Production in Einstein-Cartan Theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Introducing torsion into General Relativity leads to new four-point interactions for fermions. These are universal and must also affect any fermion dark matter. We improve existing calculations of dark matter production through the Einstein-Cartan theory four-fermion interaction by also considering the s-channel graviton exchange as another contributing process. The effect on both the total cross section as well as the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation collision term is calculated and discussed. We also introduce the Holst term, which generally modifies the four-fermion interaction coupling constant as well as introduces two new four-fermion interactions, and discuss and compute its effect on the total produced dark matter abundance.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Corrected sign of the EC interaction, 24 pages, 2 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Dymnikova spacetime replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with a de Sitter core, and its lapse deviates from Schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2M)}$. Whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. We address it with GRHD simulations of BHL accretion onto Dymnikova BH for six values of the critical length, $0.1M\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1M$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. All runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. The dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7M$. Because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. The time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3M)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0M$ and $31.6\pm0.4M)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. Accretion onto a Dymnikova BH is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. More broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Mass and angular momentum assessement of the neutron star XTEJ 1807-294 using X-ray triplets
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The X-ray power-density spectrum of the accreting millisecond pulsar XTEJ 1807-294 contains several triplets of simultaneously observed quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs): a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. This fact allows us to assess the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star. We also apply an error propagation formula to obtain interval estimates of the parameters of the star. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs. The degree of consistency of the bounds obtained with the different triplets may provide information for the viability of the used models.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 5 pages, Proceedings of the 49th international conference Applications of Mathematics in Engineering and Economics (AMEE 2023)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: First law of thermodynamics for interacting charged black holes and applications
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive a mass variation identity expressing the first law of black hole thermodynamics for asymptotically flat, stationary, axisymmetric Einstein-Maxwell solutions with multiple electrically charged horizons and finite conical axis singularities. Under the stated asymptotic and parameter regularity hypotheses, the identity holds for independent variations of all parameters within families of fixed horizon types. On the all-degenerate family, a correction to the ADM mass defines a scalar function whose derivatives with respect to angular momenta are the horizon angular velocities. At the Majumdar-Papapetrou family, its angular momentum Hessian is positive definite. Combining the first variation identity with a separate theorem on the sign of the conical parameters shows that this Hessian is nondecreasing in the positive-semidefinite order along admissible paths of increasing Weyl gaps at fixed positive charges.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory: Analytic treatment
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Non-Abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory. The onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged Reissner-Nordström black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. In the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs theory. In particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{μ_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $μ\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the Yang-Mills field due to the Higgs effect). Interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${μ_{k+1}/{μ_{k}}}=e^{-{{2π}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: No smooth real instanton saddles in self-dual Yang-Mills on AdS$_4$
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In the self-dual limit of Yang-Mills theory on Euclidean AdS$_4$ studied by Heuveline, Ruzziconi, Sheta and Strominger, the boundary condition of the second-order action becomes vacuous, but the boundary equation of the first-order action is non-trivial. We show that, with this equation, the vacuum is the only saddle with a real gauge field when both fields are smooth up to the conformal boundary, for any compact gauge group. In particular, the self-dual solutions of Sarioglu and Tekin (2009) are not saddles; we also correct their charges, which omitted a surface term at the conformal boundary. Complex saddles and singular limits remain open.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A simple flux criterion for trapped surface formation by short pulses of gravitational radiation and matter
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We discuss the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter fields, in a double-null formulation. We identify a hierarchy of orders in the pulse width for the geometric and matter quantities consistent with the evolution equations. Under the assumption that this hierarchy holds throughout the region considered, the incoming fluxes undergo approximately conservative inward transport and are thereby amplified. The Raychaudhuri equation then gives an initial flux criterion for trapped surface formation. The conditions on the matter are expressed through the Ricci components and their derivatives, which allows the argument to be developed without specifying a particular matter model.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=β\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=β(E_{\mathcal B}-Ω_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $β=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Reference-renormalized Jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We develop a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. The construction uses the fixed-energy Jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. Instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference Jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. This gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the Gauss-Bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. We prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. The method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the Riemannian Jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-Euclidean. We demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings: Schwarzschild-like bumblebee, Kottler, and Janis-Newman-Winicour (JNW) spacetimes. The formalism therefore identifies circular-orbit anchoring as an auxiliary primitive gauge choice rather than a prerequisite for finite-distance Jacobi Gauss-Bonnet deflection.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages, 1 figure. Under consideration in PRD

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8σ$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5σ$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincaré expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We analyze the gravitational-wave (GW) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a short GRB jet with parameters corresponding to those of GRB 170817A. The signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the GRBs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized Einstein equations of an MHD simulation. Separating the GW signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. The waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$Hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the GRB duration. A pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the GW signal can reveal processes deep in the GRB engine that cannot be observed otherwise. The signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. The total radiated GW energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal E}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. Comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to GW170817 are marginally detectable by DECIGO from up to 10 Mpc and by the Einstein Telescope from 1 Mpc. The injected Poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. An engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some GRB models, would substantially increase the GW energy and detectability.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Static Vacuum Geometry Encodes Gravitational Collapse and Cosmology
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that, within covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational Hamiltonian. We further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. These conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. Our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A Stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and Stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the Stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Two-loop RI/SMOM-$\overline{\text{MS}}$ matching factors for the renormalization of bi-local operators contributing to $ε_K$
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The measure of indirect CP violation in the neutral kaon system, $ε_K$, is an important precision test of the Standard Model. A first-principles Standard Model prediction of $ε_K$ requires evaluating the long-distance contribution in which the $ΔS = 2$ process proceeds via two $ΔS = 1$ operators. The non-perturbative nature of QCD in the relevant energy regimes requires a lattice QCD simulation. In this paper we present the two-loop, $O(α_s)$ RI/SMOM - $\overline{\text{MS}}$ matching factors required to renormalize a lattice QCD calculation of the long-distance contribution to $ε_K$.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Confining strings in the reconfined phase of trace deformed three dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Adding a trace deformation to the Yang-Mills action keeps the theory confining above the standard deconfinement temperature, in the so-called reconfined phase. We study the confining flux tube of the trace-deformed $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ theory in three dimensions with lattice simulations of Polyakov loop correlators.
